I am 63 years old and have farmed my land in Quzhou for 45 years. I finished high school, so I do my own sums on input costs and yields instead of guessing. My soil is alluvial loam with medium phosphorus but decent potassium, and after decades of wheat-maize double cropping, I know it gets tired if I do not feed it properly. Last year my wheat yielded 480 kg per mu, my maize yielded 580 kg, and my cotton gave 280 kg of seed cotton. This year I am pushing each crop a little harder because seed and fertilizer prices have not jumped, and with only two of us working 9 mu, a bad harvest would hurt more than wasting a few kilos of fertilizer.

My 6 mu of winter wheat is already in the ground. I planted an improved variety, Jimai 22, last October with a basal dressing of 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer. Now at jointing stage, I will topdress with 25 kg per mu of urea to bring my nitrogen to 18 kg per mu, with 7 kg of phosphorus and 6 kg of potassium total. I will irrigate four times—greening, jointing, heading, and grain filling—and spray twice, once for weeds and once for insects and scab at heading. I expect 500 kg per mu.

On my other 3 mu, I will plant hybrid Bt cotton in the next week after one pass of rotary tillage. Cotton needs more potassium or the leaves yellow in August, so I will apply 14 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 9 kg potassium per mu, using compound fertilizer and a side-dressing of potassium chloride. Cotton takes four irrigations and five pesticide sprays for bollworm, aphids, and spider mites. I am targeting 300 kg per mu of seed cotton.

After wheat harvest in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize on those same 6 mu using no-tillage direct seeding into the wheat stubble. We have only about ten days between crops, and I cannot afford to lose that window ploughing. I will apply 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu, putting down compound at sowing and spreading urea at the big trumpet stage. Maize will get three irrigations and two sprays. I expect 600 kg per mu.

I watch my neighbors closely. Most are applying similar rates this year, so I am not drifting far from the village norm. I figure my total fertilizer bill will run about 2,200 yuan across all 9 mu, which is tight but manageable. I would rather spend an extra 50 yuan per mu on fertilizer than risk a yield drop. A failed crop means borrowing money; extra fertilizer just means slightly less profit.
